name: blacklist-not-in-cache-key
body: The scan blacklist is outside the cache key, so a recorded blacklist is invisible from the store and a later warm start can reuse a graph assembled under a different blacklist. Mechanism: `rust.apg.cmd_scan` guards the current scan — the warm probe is attempted only when the current blacklist is empty — while `rust.apg.warm_prepared` requires a stored unit for every source-manifest entry (`store.candidate(...)`). A whole-file blacklist drops the file's unit, so the probe misses and falls back to the ordinary path (safe). A partial-declaration blacklist (a struct/function FQN prefix) leaves the file's unit present, and that unit is recorded from the already-filtered graph: `rust.apg.incremental.record` derives every fragment via `FileIndex::build` over the assembled (already blacklist-filtered) graph. On reuse, `rust.apg.ingest.splice_cached` inserts cached nodes/edges directly; only the spool goes through `rust.apg.ingest.is_blacklisted`. The warm start reuses the blacklist-filtered fragment verbatim. The cache key is `rust.apg.cache.ScanConfigKey`, which excludes the blacklist. `requirements.requirement.fast-project-start` AC2 holds for the same effective scan configuration — a warm start at an already-scanned commit under the same config — and that same-config warm path is correct. Cross-config warm reuse is the residual gap. `requirements.note.blacklist-not-in-cache-key` is the durable home for this limitation; folding the blacklist into `rust.apg.cache.ScanConfigKey` closes the gap, including its ordinary-incremental variant.
